location.statement: Sec. 3.1 'Closed-Form Cross-Attention Refinement', Eq. (1) (objective, eq:close-form-loss) and Eq. (2) (solution, eq:close-form-solution)
location.proof: Appendix A 'Closed-Form Solution Proof' (sec:proof), X_suppl.tex lines ~45-72

background_notation.W_k: pretrained cross-attention Key (or Value) projection matrix, in R^{d1 x d2}
background_notation.W'_k: the refined projection matrix being solved for, in R^{d1 x d2}
background_notation.e^f_i: embedding (in R^{d2}) of a word co-existing with the target phrase (i=1..n, 'mapping' terms)
background_notation.e^g_i: embedding of that same word when the target phrase is replaced by its super-category / a generic concept
background_notation.e^p_i: prior-preserving embedding (i=n+1..n+m, 'preserving' terms), by default computed on MS-COCO
background_notation.lambda_1: positive regularization hyperparameter weighting the prior-preservation terms
background_notation.n, m: number of mapping and preserving embeddings, respectively

hypotheses: The symmetric matrix G := sum_{i=1}^n e^f_i (e^f_i)^T + lambda_1 sum_{i=n+1}^{n+m} e^p_i (e^p_i)^T is invertible (the paper argues it is 'in general' positive definite; see C2).
items.statement_informal: The regularized least-squares objective L(W'_k) = sum_i ||W'_k e^f_i - W_k e^g_i||^2 + lambda_1 sum_i ||W'_k e^p_i - W_k e^p_i||^2 is minimized by W'_k = (sum W_k e^g_i (e^f_i)^T + lambda_1 sum W_k e^p_i (e^p_i)^T) (sum e^f_i (e^f_i)^T + lambda_1 sum e^p_i (e^p_i)^T)^{-1}, i.e. the ridge-regression / linear-associative-memory normal-equation solution, provided the Gram matrix G is invertible.
items.statement_formal: Minimize over W'_k in R^{d1 x d2}:  L(W'_k) = sum_{i=1}^n ||W'_k e^f_i - W_k e^g_i||_2^2 + lambda_1 sum_{i=n+1}^{n+m} ||W'_k e^p_i - W_k e^p_i||_2^2.  With A := sum_{i=1}^n W_k e^g_i (e^f_i)^T + lambda_1 sum_{i=n+1}^{n+m} W_k e^p_i (e^p_i)^T and G := sum_{i=1}^n e^f_i (e^f_i)^T + lambda_1 sum_{i=n+1}^{n+m} e^p_i (e^p_i)^T, the unique minimizer (G invertible) is W'_k = A G^{-1}.
items.proof_as_in_paper:
Differentiate L w.r.t. W'_k and set to zero:
  dL/dW'_k = 2 sum_{i=1}^n (W'_k e^f_i - W_k e^g_i)(e^f_i)^T + 2 lambda_1 sum_{i=n+1}^{n+m} (W'_k e^p_i - W_k e^p_i)(e^p_i)^T = 0.
Rearranging the mapping/preserving terms:
  sum W'_k e^f_i (e^f_i)^T + lambda_1 sum W'_k e^p_i (e^p_i)^T = sum W_k e^g_i (e^f_i)^T + lambda_1 sum W_k e^p_i (e^p_i)^T,
i.e. W'_k ( sum e^f_i (e^f_i)^T + lambda_1 sum e^p_i (e^p_i)^T ) = sum W_k e^g_i (e^f_i)^T + lambda_1 sum W_k e^p_i (e^p_i)^T. Right-multiplying by the inverse of the (symmetric, full-rank) Gram matrix gives W'_k = A G^{-1}. The paper then argues G is invertible (see C2). The same derivation applies to W'_v.
items.proof_technique: Paper: set the matrix derivative to zero -> normal equations -> right-multiply by G^{-1}. Formalization: complete the square -- prove L(W) = L(W*) + sum_i c_i ||(W-W*) a_i||^2 whenever W* G = A, which gives a global (and, under G positive definite, unique) minimizer directly and supplies the global minimality that the derivative-zero step leaves implicit.
items.proof_completeness: self-contained (given C2's invertibility); the minimality (vs. mere stationarity) is left implicit in the paper and made explicit in the formalization.
external_dependencies: Matrix calculus identity d/dW ||W a - b||^2 = 2 (W a - b) a^T (the paper uses this without citation; the formalization avoids it entirely via completing the square).
Linear-associative-memory / knowledge-editing framing (anderson1972simple, kohonen2012associative, meng2022mass, gandikota2023unified) -- conceptual, not a mathematical dependency.
known_issues_in_paper: The paper writes W_k in R^{d1 x d2} acting on embeddings e in R^{d2}, i.e. W_k e in R^{d1}; the appendix says 'e^f_i in R^{d2}'. Consistent, no issue -- recorded only to pin the dimensions (main text writes W'_k in R^{d_in x d_out}, appendix d1 x d2; these are the same object).

The paper only sets the derivative to zero; it does not separately verify the stationary point is the global minimum (true here by convexity of the quadratic, but not argued). The formalization supplies this.

Invertibility of G is argued informally ('highly improbable all terms vanish ... in general positive definite'); the precise sufficient condition is captured in C2 as an explicit non-degeneracy hypothesis.
items.formalization_notes: Prove ONE general weighted-least-squares closed form over an arbitrary finite index set with per-term weights c_i >= 0, inputs a_i in R^{d2}, targets b_i in R^{d1}. Complete-the-square identity uses only mulVec expansion + Finset.sum swaps + the componentwise normal equations (W* G = A  <->  forall r k, sum_i c_i ((W* a_i)_r - (b_i)_r)(a_i)_k = 0); no matrix-trace machinery. The closed form A G^{-1} satisfies W* G = A via Matrix.nonsing_inv_mul (needs IsUnit G.det, supplied by C2). C3 and C4 are this same theorem re-instantiated.

items.name: Gram matrix is positive semidefinite, and positive definite (invertible) under non-degeneracy
items.type: lemma (grounds the invertibility step of C1)

location.statement: Appendix A 'Closed-Form Solution Proof' (sec:proof), the paragraph 'To ensure the validity of the final step ... full rank' and the following quadratic-form display
eqs: the x^T G x = sum ||x^T e^f_i||^2 + lambda_1 sum ||x^T e^p_i||^2 >= 0 display

background_notation.G: the symmetric d2 x d2 Gram matrix sum e^f_i (e^f_i)^T + lambda_1 sum e^p_i (e^p_i)^T

hypotheses: lambda_1 >= 0 (positive in the paper; >= 0 suffices for PSD).

For positive definiteness: no nonzero x in R^{d2} is orthogonal to every e^f_i and every e^p_i with positive weight (i.e. the weighted embeddings span R^{d2}). The paper states this as 'highly improbable all terms vanish -> in general positive definite'.
items.statement_informal: For any x, x^T G x = sum_i ||x^T e^f_i||^2 + lambda_1 sum_i ||x^T e^p_i||^2 >= 0, so G is positive semidefinite; and G is positive definite (hence invertible) exactly when the embeddings span R^{d2} (no nonzero x is orthogonal to all of them).
items.statement_formal: G := sum_{i=1}^n e^f_i (e^f_i)^T + lambda_1 sum_{i=n+1}^{n+m} e^p_i (e^p_i)^T is symmetric and satisfies x^T G x = sum_i (x . e^f_i)^2 + lambda_1 sum_i (x . e^p_i)^2 >= 0 for all x (PosSemidef). If additionally, for every x != 0, some e with positive weight has x . e != 0, then x^T G x > 0 for x != 0 (PosDef), so det G > 0 and G is invertible.
items.proof_as_in_paper: For any nonzero x: x^T ( sum e^f_i (e^f_i)^T + lambda_1 sum e^p_i (e^p_i)^T ) x = sum (x^T e^f_i)(x^T e^f_i)^T + lambda_1 sum (x^T e^p_i)(x^T e^p_i)^T = sum ||x^T e^f_i||^2 + lambda_1 sum ||x^T e^p_i||^2 >= 0. Because e^p_i are computed over the large MS-COCO dataset, it is highly improbable that all terms ||x^T e^p_i||^2 vanish simultaneously, so in general the quadratic form is strictly positive for x != 0, i.e. G is positive definite and thus invertible.
items.proof_technique: Expand the quadratic form of a sum of weighted rank-1 outer products into a nonnegative-weighted sum of squared inner products; strict positivity <-> spanning (non-degeneracy) condition.
items.proof_completeness: self-contained for PSD; the PD/invertibility step replaces the paper's probabilistic 'highly improbable' phrasing with an explicit, sharp non-degeneracy hypothesis.
known_issues_in_paper: The paper's ||x^T e^p_i||^2 notation treats the scalar x^T e^p_i as a norm; harmless (||scalar||^2 = scalar^2). Recorded for fidelity.

The invertibility argument is probabilistic/informal ('highly improbable ... in general positive definite'), not a proof of a stated sufficient condition. The formalization states the exact sufficient condition (spanning) as a hypothesis and proves PD under it.
items.formalization_notes: Matrix.PosSemidef via the definition (Hermitian over R = symmetric, plus 0 <= x^T G x); each e e^T = Matrix.vecMulVec e e is symmetric and contributes c_i (e . x)^2 >= 0. PosDef under the spanning hypothesis; PosDef -> det > 0 (Matrix.PosDef.det_pos) -> IsUnit det -> invertible, which is exactly what C1's closed form consumes.

location.proof: not derived in the paper -- asserted 'Similar to Eq. (2), this optimization problem has a closed-form solution as well.'

background_notation.W_k^*: the fused projection matrix being solved for
background_notation.W'_k: the closed-form refined weight from Sec. 3.1
background_notation.Delta W_{k,i}: the LoRA modulation for the i-th erased concept
background_notation.e^f_j: embedding of a word co-existing with a target phrase (j=1..p, mapping terms)
background_notation.q, p, m, lambda_2: number of concepts; number of mapping and preserving embeddings; positive hyperparameter

hypotheses: The corresponding Gram matrix is invertible (same as C2).
items.statement_informal: Minimizing sum_{i=1}^q sum_{j=1}^p ||W_k^* e^f_j - (W'_k + Delta W_{k,i}) e^f_j||^2 + lambda_2 sum_j ||W_k^* e^p_j - W_k e^p_j||^2 has the same normal-equation closed form as C1, with targets b = (W'_k + Delta W_{k,i}) e^f_j for the mapping terms and W_k e^p_j for the preserving terms.
items.statement_formal: This is C1's general theorem instantiated with index set {(i,j)} for mapping terms and {j} for preserving terms; inputs a = e^f_j / e^p_j, targets b = (W'_k+Delta W_{k,i}) e^f_j / W_k e^p_j, weights 1 / lambda_2. The minimizer is (sum b a^T)(sum a a^T)^{-1}, the analog of Eq. (2).
items.proof_as_in_paper: Asserted by analogy to Eq. (2); no separate derivation given.
items.proof_technique: Direct instantiation of C1 (the general weighted-least-squares closed form).
items.proof_completeness: follows immediately from C1 once stated as an instance -- this is the point of proving C1 generally.
known_issues_in_paper: The paper only says 'this has a closed-form solution as well' without writing it out; the formalization makes the instance explicit and derives it from C1.
items.formalization_notes: In Instances.lean, choose the index set / a / b / c and apply C1's closed-form theorem. No new mathematics.

background_notation.lambda_3: weight for domain-specific prior knowledge (vs. lambda_1 for general prior)
background_notation.m': number of general-knowledge preserving terms (of the total m); m - m' domain-specific terms

items.statement_informal: Splitting the preservation terms into m' general + (m-m') domain-specific, weighted lambda_1 and lambda_3, gives the same closed form with a third weighted group added to both A and G.
items.statement_formal: C1's general theorem with three weight groups (weights 1, lambda_1, lambda_3); minimizer A G^{-1} as before.
items.proof_as_in_paper: Same derivation as C1 with an extra weighted sum; the paper writes the resulting formula directly.
known_issues_in_paper: The source reuses the label 'eq:close-form-fuse' for BOTH the fusion objective (rendered Eq. (7)) and this lambda_3 variant (rendered Eq. (19)) -- a duplicate LaTeX label, harmless to the rendered numbering. Recorded for fidelity.

The lambda_3 summation index in the display runs i=n+m' .. n+m, overlapping the lambda_1 index at i=n+m' (an off-by-one in the summation bounds); the intended partition is m' general + (m-m') domain-specific terms. The formalization uses the intended disjoint partition.
items.formalization_notes: Instances.lean: same as C3 with an extra weight group. No new mathematics.

location.proof: not stated in the paper (xi is defined, not proved to be a density)

background_notation.xi(t): sampling density over timestep t used when training the LoRA modules
background_notation.t_1, t_2: bounds of the high-probability interval, t_1 < t_2 (paper: 200, 400)

items.statement_informal: xi(t) = (sigma(gamma(t-t_1)) - sigma(gamma(t-t_2)))/Z >= 0 for all t, because sigma is strictly increasing and t_1 < t_2 make sigma(gamma(t-t_1)) >= sigma(gamma(t-t_2)); with Z the (positive) normalizing constant, xi is a valid probability density.
items.statement_formal: For gamma > 0, t_1 < t_2, Z > 0: for all t, 0 <= (sigma(gamma(t-t_1)) - sigma(gamma(t-t_2)))/Z, since sigma strictly monotone and gamma(t-t_1) >= gamma(t-t_2).
items.proof_as_in_paper: None -- xi is presented as a design choice, not proved to be a density.
items.proof_technique: Monotonicity of the logistic sigmoid (Real.strictMono... or via its derivative) applied to gamma(t-t_1) >= gamma(t-t_2); nonnegativity of a difference of an increasing function.
items.proof_completeness: trivial once monotonicity of sigma is invoked; included only for completeness of the paper's minor mathematical content.
external_dependencies: Monotonicity of the logistic sigmoid (available in Mathlib / provable from its derivative).
items.formalization_notes: Optional / nice-to-have (CFIS.lean). Small. Non-negativity is the clean statement; full 'integrates to 1' would need to pin Z = integral, which the paper leaves implicit.
